## A tree against every triangle for every pixel

64x32, SAH, 4 triangles a leaf. Small triangles scattered through the view, from a fixed
seed.

| Triangles | Linear | div | BVH | div | Depth | Issued | Lane work |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 | 30,804 | 15.2% | 45,982 | 58.1% | 4 | **0.67x** | 1.36x |
| 64 | 110,012 | 16.5% | 103,661 | 66.8% | 6 | **1.06x** | 2.67x |
| 256 | 425,906 | 16.6% | 322,590 | 77.6% | 9 | **1.32x** | 4.92x |
| 1024 | 1,688,782 | 16.6% | 903,148 | 82.5% | 11 | **1.87x** | 8.92x |
| 4096 | 6,724,042 | 16.5% | 2,327,000 | 85.1% | 14 | **2.89x** | 16.17x |

Lane work is what the tree removes; issued slots are what a warp keeps after
its lanes take different paths down it. The gap between the two columns is
the SIMT tax on tree traversal.

### Entering the nearer child first

| Triangles | Unordered | Nearest | Ordering |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 | 45,982 | 58,576 | **0.78x** |
| 64 | 103,661 | 150,460 | **0.69x** |
| 256 | 322,590 | 357,780 | **0.90x** |
| 1024 | 903,148 | 578,792 | **1.56x** |
| 4096 | 2,327,000 | 1,044,345 | **2.23x** |

Two slab tests at every interior node, against whole subtrees the running
best can cut off. Which wins is a property of the scene rather than of the
technique.
